london.source_family: Planning London Datahub applications and development-progress fields
london.why: Best next London source because it can convert public-page architecture milestones into row-level planning events with authority, application reference, decision/progress dates, geometry and borough scope.
london.collision_risk: high with london-architecture-public-pages and existing GLA Planning Datahub rows
london.minimum_gate: Use application reference plus LPA code as the canonical key; if missing, require same borough/site/address, same or adjacent year, and title/address token overlap before merging.

london.source_family: Planning Data official designation/constraint rows: listed-building outlines, certificate of immunity, heritage at risk, conservation areas
london.why: Highest trust for heritage/designation milestones and already visibly collides with public-page listing events.
london.minimum_gate: Canonical Planning Data entity/reference or NHLE list-entry number wins. Public-page rows become corroborating evidence, not separate events, when same list-entry/address, same designation date/year and distance <= 75 m.

london.source_family: London Development Database / strategic development pipeline archive
london.why: Fills pre-2024 development approvals/completions where current PLD coverage and public architecture pages are uneven.
london.minimum_gate: Require LDD site/application ID or exact site name plus borough plus completion/permission date type. Never merge permission, start and completion into one event.

nyc.source_family: DOB permits and certificates of occupancy
nyc.why: Best official next step for building-level lifecycle claims; supports permit/filing/CO dates without treating architecture-public-page completion copy as sole evidence.
nyc.collision_risk: high with nyc-architecture-public-pages completions and openings
nyc.minimum_gate: Use job number, BIN, BBL and permit/CO number as canonical keys. If only geometry/title match, keep as separate evidence unless date type matches exactly.

nyc.source_family: DCP ZAP project data and ZAP BBL crosswalk
nyc.why: Strongest official planning-action source for rezonings and land-use review milestones; good bridge from named public projects to lots.
nyc.collision_risk: medium with architecture pages, capital tracker and housing database project rows
nyc.minimum_gate: Merge only on ZAP project ID or ULURP/application number. Lot/BBL proximity alone is a candidate flag, not a duplicate.

nyc.source_family: LPC landmark and LPC permit application data
nyc.why: Current collisions show LPC data can canonicalize landmark designation events and preserve formal landmark/permit IDs.
nyc.minimum_gate: LPC landmark ID/designation report number wins; public-page rows become corroboration when same landmark name/address, designation year and distance <= 50 m.

belfast.source_family: NI Planning Portal / Belfast planning applications and decisions
belfast.why: Highest value because Belfast needs application-reference-level gates; current planning-statistics rows are numerous but collide spatially with unrelated architecture milestones.
belfast.collision_risk: very high false-positive risk near dense city-centre sites
belfast.minimum_gate: Application reference is mandatory for merge. Without LA04/reference match, require exact address token overlap and same date type; distance alone must never merge.

belfast.source_family: Belfast City Council open data and official facility/project pages
belfast.why: Best source family for civic facilities, leisure centres, markets, parks and public realm projects currently represented as curated milestones.
belfast.minimum_gate: Official project/facility URL plus normalized facility name plus same opening/completion year should merge into one event with multiple evidence links.

belfast.source_family: DfC Historic Environment Division listed buildings / HED notifications and Translink/DfI project evidence
belfast.why: Canonicalizes heritage and transport/station claims where public-page architecture rows already overlap with official transport/facility rows.
belfast.collision_risk: high for station openings and listing notifications
belfast.minimum_gate: Use HED record number or transport project/station identifier where present. Merge public-page rows only when same named asset, same effective event type, same year and distance <= 75 m.

hard_duplicate: Same city_id and same canonical source record id: application reference, permit number, CO number, ZAP project id, LPC landmark id, NHLE/list-entry id, HED record id, or official project URL.
Same city_id, same normalized source URL, and same source_record_id regardless of title wording.
Same city_id, same normalized title/address, same effective date precision/value, same event type, and point distance <= 25 m when no canonical id exists.
soft_duplicate_candidate: Same city_id and year, point distance <= 100 m, and title/address token similarity >= 0.35.
Same city_id and same site/facility name within +/- 1 year where one source is a public-page milestone and the other is an official administrative record.
Same property identifier family, e.g. BBL/BIN/UPRN/address, but different source date fields.
do_not_merge_without_review: Planning approval/permission, construction start, completion, certificate of occupancy, opening, listing/designation and funding/budget decisions are different event types even at the same site.
OSM edit/change dates are not real-world construction dates and must stay separate unless corroborated by an official effective date.
Planning-statistics rows near a landmark or project are not duplicates unless the application reference or exact address/title tokens agree.
Multiple buildings in one row/block, e.g. Tin Pan Alley or large campuses, need parent-child grouping rather than blind point-distance merging.

notes: Counts are current generated/corpus counts, not claims of complete civic coverage.

Soft collision counts are audit heuristics over same-city/year architecture-public-page rows versus current official-ish planning/heritage/project source families; examples are for gating design, not automatic merge decisions.
The next ingestion pass should prefer canonical official IDs, then attach public-page records as corroborating evidence where dates and event type agree.
